candidates.name: Report material volume for a library
candidates.explanation: The system should provide a report showing the volume of material associated with a specified library. The report must support determining the volume at any point in time, including the current volume.
candidates.evidence:
The system should provide the ability to report on the volume of material
in a given library at any point in time

candidates.name: Count all items assigned to the selected library
candidates.explanation: The volume calculation should count all items whose location matches the selected library, rather than limiting the count to items currently checked in or otherwise available.
candidates.evidence: Counts all items with a location = your library

candidates.name: Include new acquisitions in volume reporting
candidates.explanation: The report should account for newly acquired items as one of the material-volume components.
candidates.evidence:
The system should provide the ability to report on the volume of material
in a given library at any point in time, based on:
- New acquisitions

candidates.name: Include checked-in items in volume reporting
candidates.explanation: The report should account for items currently on the shelf, meaning items that are checked in, as one of the material-volume components.

candidates.name: Include checked-out items in volume reporting
candidates.explanation: The report should account for items out in circulation, meaning items that are checked out, as one of the material-volume components.

candidates.name: Show separate status counts and a total
candidates.explanation: The report should provide the total volume along with separate counts for new acquisitions, items on the shelf, and items out in circulation, so that these components can be reviewed independently as well as together.
candidates.evidence:
I think Maria is asking for all three counts separately plus a total. That
makes sense for collection management.

candidates.name: Break down volume by category
candidates.explanation: The report should support category-based breakdowns of volume, including examples such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books, rather than presenting only one aggregate count.
candidates.evidence:
The report should allow breaking down volume in categories such as:
- Total items in library
- Number of holds
- Number of adult fiction
- Number of board books
- Other customizable categories

candidates.name: Support customizable reporting categories
candidates.explanation: Libraries should be able to configure the categories used for volume breakdowns because different libraries may require different classifications. The discussion also identifies examples such as fiction/non-fiction and format.
candidates.evidence:
Can we make the categories customizable? Different libraries
might want different breakdowns.

candidates.name: Show holds counts by category
candidates.explanation: The report should show the number of holds for each applicable category, in addition to providing category-level volume counts.
candidates.evidence: Shows breakdowns with holds count per category

candidates.name: Filter volume by date
candidates.explanation: The report should support date filters so users can calculate volume at a selected point in time instead of being limited to the current volume.
candidates.evidence:
We can also add date filters - volume at any point in time, not just
current.

candidates.name: Support historical volume comparisons
candidates.explanation: The reporting capability should make it possible to compare volume across historical points in time, supporting historical analysis rather than only a current snapshot.
candidates.evidence: This would be useful for historical comparisons.

candidates.name: Use acquisition date for volume-change reporting
candidates.explanation: The system should use the tracked acquisition date to support reports showing how volume changes over time, including the amount of volume added during a specified period.
candidates.evidence:
Yes, the database tracks acquisition date for items. We can definitely
build reports that show volume changes over time.

candidates.name: Filter recent additions by configurable time windows
candidates.explanation: The report should support viewing how much volume was added within recent time windows such as the last 30, 60, or 90 days. These intervals are proposed as useful reporting options.
candidates.evidence:
It would
be helpful to see how much volume has been added in the last 30/60/90 days.
